text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Gerard Sanderink, who has made takeover bid for info technology firm Multihouse, promises firm management hand. (p1)
- Financial services group Achmea and social security administration group GAK plan three joint ventures. (p1)
- Niko Wijnolst, chairman of small businesses association MKB, resigns after disagreements within the board. (p1)
- Switch from the guilder to the Euro in 2002 could be implemented in just two weeks. (p1)
- Truck maker Scania might slash 300 jobs at its Dutch plant in Zwolle. (p3)
- Philips sells its 25 pct stake in Danish audio-visual electronics firm Bang & Olufsen. (p3)
- Chairman of transport group Hapag Lloyd denies P&O Nedlloyd has a stake in his company. (p3)
- U.S. president Bill Clinton arrives in Netherlands to commemorate Marshall Plan. (p1)
- Sanitary ware producer Sphinx Gustavsberg sells its tile division. (p2)
- Finance Ministry's tight control of slot machine producers brings in an extra 400 million guilders in taxes. (p2) DE TELEGRAAF
- Image of Queen Beatrix will not appear on Euro notes. (p1)
- KLM Royal Dutch Airlines misses out on 100 million guilder maintenance order from McDonnell Douglas to modernise 23 DC-10 aircraft. (p23)
- Dordtsche Petroleum -- holding company for Royal Dutch Petroleum shares -- will continue to offer stock dividends which are exempt from personal income tax. (p25) ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Foreign affairs minister Hans van Mierlo says Europe and U.S. should make binding agreements to coordinate policy on human rights. (p1)
- Economic Affairs Minister Hans Wijers wants to make a final attempt to bring about an agreement on liberalising the European gas market. (p15)
